title: How to Pass a Funded Challenge Without Blowing It
question: How do I pass a funded trading challenge and actually keep the account?
angle: Most traders fail funded challenges not because of bad strategy but because they trade the challenge differently than they trade in real life. Harvest breaks down the exact process discipline, risk rules, and mindset shifts that separate traders who pass from those who reset for the fifth time.

title: Best ICT Trading Course: What to Look For vs. Hype
question: What is the best ICT trading course I can take to actually learn and profit?
angle: After 10+ years coaching struggling traders, Harvest breaks down what separates a course that builds a real edge from one that just sells concepts. Contrarian take: the 'best' course is rarely the most popular one.

title: Trading Coach vs Trading Course: Which Do You Need?
question: Should I get a trading coach or just buy a course?
angle: Both are legitimate at different stages. Give the course option real credit: it is far cheaper and correct when you cannot yet state your entry criteria in one sentence. Coaching earns its price only once you can state them and still break them.

title: What to Ask a Trading Coach Before You Pay
question: What questions should I ask a trading coach before paying?
angle: Four questions that expose a bad fit in one conversation: can I watch you trade live, what did your worst month look like, what happens in a session, and how many students stop showing up. Explain what good and bad answers sound like.
targetKeyword: questions to ask a trading coach

title: Trading Mentorship Red Flags That Cost Traders Thousands
question: How do I avoid getting scammed by a trading mentor?
angle: Concrete disqualifiers: guaranteed returns, urgency to decide today, income screenshots as primary proof, refusal to discuss losing months, signals sold as education. Explain why each one correlates with a bad product.

title: Signals Groups vs Real Trading Coaching
question: Is a signals group the same as trading coaching?
angle: Signals give you a fish and create dependency; coaching builds your own decision process. Be fair: signals can be useful for observing entries if you journal the reasoning. The failure mode is treating them as education.

title: Are You Actually Ready for a Trading Coach?
question: When should I get a trading coach?
angle: A readiness test rather than a sales pitch. If you have no journal, no traded method, or would pay from trading capital, you are not ready and should be told so plainly.
targetKeyword: when to get a trading coach

title: Group Coaching vs One-on-One: Which Fits Your Stage?
question: Is group trading coaching or one on one better?
angle: Group wins on price, structure and accountability. One-on-one wins only where your specific errors need catching. Map each to the stage it suits instead of declaring a winner.
targetKeyword: group trading coaching vs one on one

title: Does Coaching Improve Prop Firm Pass Rates?
question: Does coaching help you pass a prop firm challenge?
angle: Most challenge failures come from breaking daily loss limits while recovering, not from bad setups. That is a behaviour problem, which is the specific thing coaching addresses. No guarantees, and say so.

title: Can a Trading Coach Make You Profitable?
question: Can trading coaching help me become profitable?
angle: Answer honestly: no one can promise profitability and anyone who does is disqualified. What a coach does is shorten the feedback loop and stop repeated expensive errors. Screen time and discipline stay on the trader.
targetKeyword: can a trading coach make you profitable
